51891647.question: A lent maker asks to withdraw and the call reverts. What has happened?
51891647.answer: The funds are lent out and capacity is not there to return them right now
options: Their order was already filled
They are trying to leave before a mandatory lock expires
The funds are lent out and capacity is not there to return them right now

B790047A.question: What does a single Everything contract hold?
B790047A.answer: One reserve that prices swaps, is lent out, and backs resting orders
options: One reserve that prices swaps, is lent out, and backs resting orders
Three separate pools, one per market
A reserve for swaps, and an external money market for credit
Only the order book, with swaps routed elsewhere

A9851B90.question: Why can Everything lend against tokens a normal money market refuses?
A9851B90.answer: The pool that sets the price is the pool holding the collateral, so exit liquidity is known

It uses several oracles instead of one

It insures every loan with an external fund

C27F29F6.question: What are the protocol’s only inputs?
options: An oracle feed and a keeper network
Deposits, trades, and the clock
Governance votes and a price committee
Chainlink plus an emergency multisig

9FFA7B61.question: Where does the swap price come from?
9FFA7B61.answer: From how much of each token the pool is holding, through an invariant

It is imported from the deepest external venue

D3C4FA81.question: What funds the repeg, when the pool re-centres its liquidity?
options: Retained fees only, never principal
A slice of every borrower’s collateral
The protocol treasury
Newly minted LP shares

0A445351.question: The whitepaper bounds the curve’s amplification parameter A to:
options: It gives no value at all
0 to 1

options: The same flat fee as any other
A higher fee than one that restores the balance
No fee at all
A fee set by the maker it fills

Charges a fee on withdrawals

4ACE7517.question: In what order is a swap filled?
4ACE7517.answer: Stale walls, then in-path walls, then the curve residual
options: The curve first, then any leftover orders
Stale walls, then in-path walls, then the curve residual
Oldest resting order first, regardless of price

2FEBA208.question: When is the taker’s fee decided?
2FEBA208.answer: Once up front, on the gross input and the pre-swap state
options: After the routing, on whatever actually touched the curve
Per wall filled, negotiated with each maker
Once up front, on the gross input and the pre-swap state

C944BDDE.question: Someone who buys the dip seconds after a crash pays:
C944BDDE.answer: A premium, because the curve leg executes on the displaced anchor
options: A premium, because the curve leg executes on the displaced anchor
Nothing extra, the price is the price
A discount, as a reward for adding liquidity

8051DCC3.question: A non-lent maker’s filled order is:
8051DCC3.answer: Set aside senior-most at fill time, never gated in any state
options: Credited to their balance like any other payout
Held back until the pool reaches full capacity
Paid out only after every borrower has repaid
Set aside senior-most at fill time, never gated in any state

527C4C51.question: What can block a non-lent maker from cancelling?
527C4C51.answer: Nothing at all, in any pool state
options: High utilisation on the borrowed side
Nothing at all, in any pool state
A pending liquidation tick
A governance timelock

A3694971.question: A liquidity order’s return comes from:
A3694971.answer: The rebate on each flip, since the round trip is value-neutral
options: The spread between its two legs
Interest earned while it waits
The rebate on each flip, since the round trip is value-neutral

3270691E.question: What does ticking the "lend" flag on a resting order cost you?
3270691E.answer: The cancel is no longer free or immediate
options: The cancel is no longer free or immediate
A slice of the principal, taken up front
The right to be filled at your exact price

733FFF8D.question: Can the supply index L be cut to absorb bad debt?
options: Yes, pro-rata across all suppliers
Yes, but only above a governance threshold
Only during an emergency stop
Never, under any circumstance

2F98DDE5.question: A lent exit that does not fit the capacity envelope results in:
2F98DDE5.answer: The transaction reverting intact, to be retried later

The transaction reverting intact, to be retried later
A queue position with a guaranteed date

540C6A41.question: Once an order is placed with the lend flag, the flag is:

Automatically dropped when utilisation gets high
Frozen for the life of the order
Reset at every price crossing

73AC57A4.question: Who chooses the price at which a loan gets liquidated?
options: Governance, per pair
An oracle, from the external market
The borrower, at the open

D18FF343.answer: It drifts against the borrower as interest compounds
options: It drifts against the borrower as interest compounds
It stays exactly where it was set
It drifts in the borrower’s favour

06A558EB.question: At liquidation, what is handed back to the borrower?
06A558EB.answer: Nothing, the whole tick’s collateral is seized
options: Whatever exceeds the debt plus the penalty
Nothing, the whole tick’s collateral is seized
Half of the posted collateral

382903EE.question: Does the protocol attach a stop-loss to a loan?
options: Yes, at a configurable level
Yes, automatically at the tick buffer
Only for leveraged positions

703A0FA8.question: The gate c ≥ swapIn(q) exists so that:

options: Borrowing is never cheaper than simply swapping

1845678F.question: What plays the role of a funding rate for a leveraged position?
options: An eight-hour index, like a perp venue
The kinked borrow interest rate
A fee charged on the collateral

6A8E4A53.question: Is there a hard maximum leverage?

81E02F7D.question: What does the pair’s own flash loan cost?

0.09 %, like Aave

2193669F.answer: Last, the junior tranche that absorbs losses first

Second, just under the fill claims
Third, level with lent suppliers

80C7AC4A.question: What does one LP position earn that siloed designs force you to choose between?
80C7AC4A.answer: Swap fees and lending interest, both at once

Trading fees and a governance token

1089162C.answer: Nothing, it collapses to zero width

87EFCFB5.answer: Honest liquidations lag the market too

Ten thousand times more
Roughly the square root of the count

The first liquidator to call it, via a bounty

options: Exactly 1 %
